messages.subject: [R-sig-Fedora] Request for RPMs of the latest R 4 version supported on RHEL 7.6
messages.subject_clean: Request for RPMs of the latest R 4 version supported on RHEL 7.6
messages.body_plain:
Dear Red Hat Support,
I am currently working with a system running RHEL 7.6 and would like to install the latest stable version of R 4 that is officially supported on this platform. Based on my research through CRAN, EPEL, and other repositories, it appears that R 4.3.1 is the last version available as RPMs for RHEL 7.
Unfortunately, migrating to RHEL 8 or 9 is not an option in our current environment. I am therefore looking for a way to install R 4.3.1 using RPM packages compatible with RHEL 7.6.
Could you please confirm:
? Whether R 4.3.1 is indeed the final version of R 4 supported on RHEL 7.6?? If there is an official channel or recommended procedure to obtain and install these RPMs?? Whether any alternatives exist within Red Hat support to maintain an up-to-date R environment without upgrading the operating system?

Thank you in advance for your assistance and guidance.
Best regards,Haithem KHELFAEmployee at Orange

messages.subject: [R-sig-Fedora]  Request for RPMs of the latest R 4 version supported on RHEL 7.6
messages.subject_clean: Request for RPMs of the latest R 4 version supported on RHEL 7.6
messages.body_plain:
You can use 'rig' to install any version of R on RHEL7, see
https://github.com/r-lib/rig?tab=readme-ov-file#id-rhel-fedora-rocky-linux-almalinux-etc-rpm-package

We also publish a docker container based on centos-7 and the latest R
that you can test like so:

   docker run -it ghcr.io/r-devel/centos-7

The source for this container is:
https://github.com/r-devel/containers/blob/main/centos-7/Dockerfile

Also, Haithem, please note that this is NOT Red Hat Support. This is a
mailing list run by CRAN for people using Fedora/EPEL RPMs, where some
volunteers like Jeroen and myself may chime in. If your employer pays for
extended support and you are looking for official support, this is not the
proper channel.

Best,
I?aki
